appraisal_events.evidence: comme le grand peintre que j'avais connu à Balbec, Elstir, avait trouvé le motif de deux tableaux qui se valent, dans un bâtiment scolaire sans caractère et dans une cathédrale qui est, par elle-même, un chef-d'oeuvre
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits Elstir with the same order of genius he is attributing to Berma: the ability to produce equally masterful work from a trivial subject as from an intrinsically great one, independent of the nobility of his material.

status_effects.explanation: Elstir is affirmed as a genuine artistic genius, invoked by the narrator as a positive analogy that illuminates Berma's own greatness, though the passage's primary focus remains on Berma.

ambiguities: The 'le peintre' who 'dissout maison, charrette, personnages, dans quelque grand effet de lumière' is anaphoric to the previously named Elstir, not a distinct character, though the alias map lists them as separate canonical entries; both mentions are treated here as referring to Elstir alone.

Gilberte is mentioned twice only as an analogy for the narrator's pattern of desire-driven disappointment; this is essayistic self-reflection about the narrator's psychology, not a staged evaluative event involving Gilberte, so she was not scored.
Le narrateur appears throughout only as the perceiving/reflecting consciousness analyzing aesthetic experience, never as a staged social participant, so he was not scored per the instructions.
